data.name: Lydiana
data.gender_notes: Lydiana is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'lydos' meaning 'people' or 'nation'. In Greek mythology, Lydia was an ancient kingdom in Asia Minor, known for its wealth and culture. In Christian tradition, Lydiana represents a loyal and devoted woman. The name Lydiana carries the meaning “Loyal woman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lydiana usually hope their child will grow to embody loyal woman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Lydiana belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Loyal woman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lydiana total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

Lydiana's name carries the legacy of a powerful and prosperous civilization, inspiring us to value our heritage and cultivate a appreciation for the past.

Lydiana is a name that encourages us to live purposefully and supportively, making a positive impact on those around us and in the world.

biblical_reference.note: Lydia is mentioned as a region, and a woman named Lydia is a biblical figure

historical_references.reference: Lydiana was a name given to a 7th-century AD Visigothic queen who ruled the Kingdom of Toledo in Spain.
historical_references.context: During this time, the Visigoths were the predominant group in the region, and Lydiana's rule signified the political and religious influence of the Christianized Visigothic dynasty in the Iberian Peninsula.

historical_references.reference: Another Lydiana existed during the Roman Empire, around the 3rd century AD. This Lydiana was a renowned martyr who was venerated for her devotion to Christianity during a time when the religion was persecuted.
historical_references.context: Christianity was a minority religion during the Roman Empire, and the persecution of Christians was a common occurrence. Lydiana's martyrdom served as an inspiration to many and contributed to the spread of Christianity in the Roman Empire.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Lydiana is of European origin and has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts. In the realm of European history, it is a popular choice for characters in historical reenactment and role-playing events. In fantasy literature, Lydiana is a name that evokes a sense of mystery and adventure, often used for characters in epic tales or high fantasy novels. Lastly, in the world of role-playing games, Lydiana is a common name for player-created characters in Tabletop Simulator and World of Warcraft, reflecting its historical and fantastical appeal.
